title: Strict Kan enriched models of coherent space valued bimodules
statement: Use the nested universe, quasicategory, coherent functor, simplicial model category and homotopy coherent nerve conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] and [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams], and the space category $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal U})$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Let $C$ and $D$ be small infinity-categories and let $H:C^{\mathrm{op}}\times D\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ be a small-space-valued coherent functor. There are Bergner cofibrant locally Kan simplicial categories $A$ and $B$, equivalences $N_{\mathrm{hc}}A\simeq C$ and $N_{\mathrm{hc}}B\simeq D$, and a strict simplicial functor $M:A^{\mathrm{op}}\times B\to\mathsf{sSet}$ whose values are $\mathcal U$-small Kan complexes, together with a coherent equivalence between the coherent nerve $N_{\mathrm{hc}}M:N_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)^{\mathrm{op}}\times N_{\mathrm{hc}}B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ and $H$ transported along these endpoint equivalences. Under this equivalence the two enriched actions of $A$ and $B$ are the first-variable precomposition and second-variable postcomposition actions of $H$, including their units, composition simplices, and all higher coherences. The choices are natural in $H$, in endpoint functors, and in additional small simplicial parameters.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.1.2, Corollary 2.2.5.6 (rigidification of products), Theorem 2.2.5.1 and Proposition 4.2.4.4 with Appendix A.3.3, combined with the Bergner model structure and the enriched diagram presentation; this two-variable strictification is an agent-formulated consequence. Archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Start with the rigidifications of the given small quasicategories. The Bergner model structure and the coherent-nerve Quillen equivalence in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] give cofibrant replacements of the rigidifications. Factor each such cofibrant object to the terminal simplicial category as a trivial cofibration followed by a fibration; the target remains cofibrant and its mapping simplicial sets are Kan. The derived coherent nerve therefore supplies equivalences N_{\mathrm{hc}}A\simeq C and N_{\mathrm{hc}}B\simeq D. Use the functorial factorizations, so these endpoint choices vary coherently with endpoint functors.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.1.2 and Theorem 2.2.5.1; Bergner model structure and coherent-nerve Quillen equivalence

proof.text: Put K=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)^{\mathrm{op}}\times N_{\mathrm{hc}}B and I=A^{\mathrm{op}}\times B. The product rigidification comparison of [lem-coef-joyal-homotopy-exponentials], followed by the counit comparison for locally Kan simplicial categories in [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification], gives a Dwyer--Kan equivalence u:\mathfrak C[K]\to I. Transport H along the endpoint equivalences from Step 1 to a coherent K-diagram p:K\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.6 and Proposition 4.2.4.4; product rigidification and transport along equivalences

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams] and [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] with the Kan simplicial model category of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], with index I and the Dwyer--Kan equivalence u. Its strict enriched presentation of p gives an enriched functor F:I\to\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal U} presenting p. Take a projectively cofibrant replacement followed by a projective fibrant replacement and call the resulting diagram M. Projective fibrations are objectwise, so every M(a,b) is a Kan complex; the fixed universe makes these values \mathcal U-small. The coherent-nerve comparison in the same theorem gives a coherent equivalence N_{\mathrm{hc}}M\simeq p, hence with H after the endpoint transport.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 and Appendix A.3.3; enriched diagram presentation

proof.text: Because M is an enriched functor on A^{\mathrm{op}}\times B, its structure maps are strict maps A(a\prime,a)\times M(a,b)\to M(a\prime,b) and M(a,b)\times B(b,b\prime)\to M(a,b\prime), with the enriched identity and composition equations. The evaluation and coherent-composition clause of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams] identifies these maps, including every transformation simplex, with first-variable precomposition and second-variable postcomposition for p and hence for H. Thus the coherent equivalence preserves both actions, their units, composition simplices, and all higher coherences.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1; enriched evaluation and coherent composition

proof.text: All choices used above are functorial replacements and enriched diagram constructions. The naturality clauses of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] and [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams] therefore make the endpoint equivalences, M, and the comparison natural in H, in maps of endpoint infinity-categories, and in any additional small simplicial parameter. Empty categories, empty values, and the point-valued case are included because the same model structures and functorial replacements apply without a nonemptiness hypothesis.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 2.2.1.2, Corollary 2.2.5.6, Theorem 2.2.5.1 and Proposition 4.2.4.4; explicit two-variable strictification
